section: Iterate — change: R1c-1 new-then-old lookup in path()
title: path() looks in .shipwright/config/ first and refuses a broken layout (R1c-1)
context: Campaign root-files-into-config: R3 moves the root shipwright_* files into .shipwright/config/ and leaves a pointer stub at the old run_config path. Readers must find a file in either place, and a half-done or doubled move must never be read silently.
decision: path() calls a new sibling module, shipwright_layout.locate: a stub at the new path, a too-new or edited root stub, a root stub without its new copy, or two regular copies (identical ones too) raise LayoutError(Exception) with the file, both paths and the fix; otherwise the new copy wins, else the root. Only regular files count; the root head is read at most 2 KiB (64 KiB for a signature-led file). No second lock; the legacy root lock stays the one lock until R3 decides again.
consequences: Nothing creates .shipwright/config/ yet, so unmigrated repos resolve exactly as before (pinned by a repo-wide guard test). The Stop hook reports a LayoutError on stderr; the 12 resolver-only hooks also need the two sibling files in the cache. Hook-by-hook handling of LayoutError is R1e; constants and carriers are R1c-2.
rationale: One lookup in the resolver reaches every reader at once (R1b routed them through path()); failing loudly on two copies is safer than guessing which one is current.
rejected: A dual lock from R1 (architecture reviewers: unneeded before R3, adds leak and timeout paths; operator chose to drop it); comparing contents to accept identical copies (breaks after the first write, can block on FIFOs); inlining the lookup in shipwright_paths (300-line cap).
